---
title: "repdist: homology-aware beta diversity for metaproteomics"
---

<style>
.main-container img { max-width: 620px; display: block; margin: 1.5em auto 0.5em; }
.caption-note { color: #b52b27; }
</style>

`repdist` represents each sample as an abundance-weighted distribution over
protein embeddings from a frozen protein language model, and compares samples
by **maximum mean discrepancy** under an RBF kernel. The ground distance is
defined for any sequence — including proteins with no tree position and no
annotation — so a metaproteome can be compared without first resolving it to
known accessions.

![](figures/simulation-pcoa.png)

<span class="caption-note">Two groups of simulated samples differing by
*function*, carried on non-overlapping homologs.</span> MMD, a structure tree
and structural bins all separate them. Protein-level Bray-Curtis, which can
only ask whether two samples hold the same accession, sees nothing. Built in
`vignette("simulation", package = "repdist")`.

# Installation

`repdist` is an R package. Install the development version from GitHub:

```r
if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("Yixuan39/repdist")
```

Embeddings run through a pinned `basilisk` Python environment, so no manual
Python setup is needed. The default ground metric is TM-Vec: cosine distance
between two protein embeddings approximates `1 - predicted TM-score`.

```r
library(repdist)

seqs <- read_fasta("proteins.fasta")
Z <- embed_proteins(seqs, model = "tmvec")

D <- sample_repdist(counts, Z)          # RBF-MMD between samples
vegan::adonis2(D ~ condition, data = meta)

G <- repdist_matrix(Z)                  # 1 - predicted TM-score
bins <- bin_proteins(G, min_sim = 0.7)  # structural bins for biomarkers
```

Two vignettes ship with the package: `vignette("repdist")` walks the workflow
on a package data subset, `vignette("simulation")` builds the figure above.

# Analyses

These are the full re-analyses behind the method, run on complete protein sets
rather than the package subsets. Each one is a standalone report.

**[Data curation](data_curation.html)** — Extended Data Table 1 of
Blakeley-Ruiz *et al.*, *ISME J* **19**(1) wraf048, from spectral counts and
inline sequences to a phyloseq object, checked against the published PERMANOVA
before anything downstream runs.

**[Case study: mouse faecal metaproteomes](case_study.html)** — six dietary
protein sources. MMD beta diversity and PERMANOVA, structural bins at predicted
TM-score 0.7, DESeq2 on the bins, and a functional reading of the most
responsive annotated bins, on every protein retained after rarefaction and a
3,000 aa length ceiling.

**[Case study 2: marine plastic substrates](case_study2.html)** — three
incubations each across four plastics, two PHBH formulations, filter paper and
ambient sediment; PLA dropped for inconsistent depth. The same four-step
workflow on a community whose proteins are largely unannotated.

**[Case study 2: annotation-oriented clustering](case_study2_annotation_report.html)** —
which clustering setting groups the plastic-substrate catalog best for
annotation: complete linkage across TM thresholds against MCL, DBSCAN\*/DBSCAN
and HDBSCAN, scored on KO and on the paper's own broad and detailed function
labels.

<span class="caption-note">The clustering report is kept as a record.</span>
The MCL, DBSCAN\*/DBSCAN and HDBSCAN options it compares have since been removed
from `bin_proteins()`, which now cuts a complete-linkage tree and nothing else.
That report's own conclusion is the reason.

# Reproducing

The sources for every report live in `inst/scripts/` on the
[`gh-pages` branch](https://github.com/Yixuan39/repdist/tree/gh-pages/inst/scripts)
and expect to run from a `repdist` checkout with the study inputs under `data/`:

```
inst/scripts/data_curation.Rmd                    # -> data/test_study/ps.rds
inst/scripts/case_study.Rmd
inst/scripts/case_study2.Rmd
inst/scripts/case_study2_annotation_report.Rmd
inst/scripts/build_trees.R                        # k-mer and TM-Vec trees
inst/scripts/case_study2_annotation.R             # -> results/case_study2_annotation_clustering/
inst/scripts/case_study_bin_ordination.R
```

The study inputs are not redistributed here; each report names the files it
reads and the accession they come from. Run `data_curation.Rmd` first — the
case studies read the phyloseq object it writes. The annotation clustering
report reads `results/case_study2_annotation_clustering/`, written by
`case_study2_annotation.R`.
